title: Dot Product of Two Sparse Vectors
hints: The vectors can have a billion dimensions, so expanding either one into a dense list is out of the question. Only indices present in both lists can contribute to the sum.
Both lists are sorted by index. Think about how merging two sorted lists lets you find all shared indices in one simultaneous pass.

When one vector has far fewer non-zeros than the other, walking the long list is wasted work; consider searching the long list for each entry of the short one instead, so the cost depends mostly on the short length.
